mainTopic: How the wording of a נדר of נזירות, including extra words, can create a second full term
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the previous משנה. That משנה ruled that someone who says 'I am a נזיר and one hour' or 'and one and a half' is a נזיר for two full terms, and the גמרא explains why both cases had to be taught. Then a new משנה teaches that 'thirty days and one hour' makes him a נזיר for thirty-one days, because נזירות is never counted in hours. רב limits this ruling: it applies only when he said 'thirty-one days' as one number. If he said 'thirty days and one day,' he is a נזיר for two terms. The גמרא explains that רב follows רבי עקיבא, who learns meaning from extra words. As proof it quotes a משנה about selling a house. There רבי עקיבא agrees that the extra words 'except for these,' said about the pit and cistern, let the seller keep a path to them without buying one.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed both 'one hour' and 'one and a half'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the earlier משנה had to teach both cases. From 'one hour' alone, we might think the 'one and a half' case is different, because there he was being exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה had taught only 'one hour,' you might say he gets two terms because he was not speaking exactly. But with 'one and a half,' where he is speaking exactly, you might say he should not count two full terms. So the משנה teaches that in all these cases he is a נזיר for two terms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why the earlier משנה listed two similar cases. Each case teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One hour' is vague, so we could understand why it turns into a whole extra term. 'One and a half' sounds exact, so we might think he only takes on 45 days. The משנה rules that even the exact-sounding version gives two full terms of thirty days each.

keyTerms.meaning: he goes into exact detail; he means a precise amount
I might say; introduces a mistaken first thought
it comes to teach us
all of them; all these cases

steps.whatToRemember: Whether he says 'one hour' or 'one and a half,' any partial extra amount means a second full term of נזירות.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only 'one hour,'
that is because he did not go into exact detail.
But 'one and a half,'
where he does go into exact detail,
I might say he should not count two,
phrases.notes: He means two full terms. You might think he only needs a term and a half, which is 45 days.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that in all of them
he is a נזיר for two terms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation, begun on the previous amud (7a), of why the משנה needed both cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each case teaches something the other case could not teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With 'one and a half,' which sounds exact, he might take on only 45 days.
steps.terutzMaskana: In every case of a partial extra amount, he observes two full terms of נזירות.

steps.title: משנה: Thirty days and one hour becomes thirty-one days
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a person who says 'thirty days and one hour' becomes a נזיר for thirty-one days, because נזירות cannot be counted in hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'I am hereby a נזיר for thirty days and one hour,' he is a נזיר for thirty-one days, because there is no נזירות for hours.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a case where someone adds a small amount of time to a thirty-day נזירות. The extra hour is rounded up to a full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזירות is counted only in whole days, so the extra hour turns into one more full day. Notice the difference from the earlier case: here the extra time is added to a stated number of days, so it becomes a 31st day and not a second term.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר; the words that make the vow
one hour
there is no נזירות for hours; it works only in whole days

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 1. 'A נזיר and one hour' means two terms, but 'thirty days and one hour' is a single term of thirty-one days.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
'I am hereby a נזיר for thirty days
and one hour,'
he is a נזיר for thirty-one days,
because there is no נזירות for hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם וְשָׁעָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Thirty days and one hour' gives a נזירות of thirty-one days, since an hour is rounded up to a full day.

steps.title: רב: Only 'thirty-one days' gives one term; 'thirty days and one day' gives two
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the משנה's thirty-one-day ruling. It applies only when the person said 'thirty-one days' as one number. If he said 'thirty days and one day,' he becomes a נזיר for two terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: They taught this only when he said 'thirty-one days.' But if he said 'thirty days and one day,' he is a נזיר for two terms.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains when the משנה's thirty-one-day ruling applies. How the person words the number makes a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'thirty-one days' as one number gives one longer term. Saying 'thirty days' and then separately 'and one day' splits it into a full thirty-day term plus the start of a new one, which grows into a second full term.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only in the case of; limits a ruling
thirty-one days, said as one number
thirty days and one day, said as two separate parts

steps.whyThisMatters: The exact wording of a נדר can change the הלכה, even when the total number of days sounds the same.

phrases.english: GEMARA: רב said:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's ruling that he is a נזיר for thirty-one days.

phrases.english: when he said 'thirty-one days,'
but if he said 'thirty days and one day,'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: he is a נזיר for two terms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's ruling to one particular wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Thirty-one days' gives one term, while 'thirty days and one day' gives two terms.

steps.title: רב follows רבי עקיבא, who learns from extra words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב's ruling is based on the view of רבי עקיבא, who holds that extra, unneeded words carry added meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds like רבי עקיבא, who learns meaning from extra language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the source of רב's ruling. This sets up the next discussion about רבי עקיבא's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He could have simply said 'thirty-one days.' Splitting it into 'thirty days and one day' uses extra words, and רבי עקיבא learns that extra words show he meant to add something, here a second term.

keyTerms.meaning: holds in line with the view of
learns meaning from; explains
extra, unneeded wording

steps.whatToRemember: רב's two-term ruling stands on רבי עקיבא's rule that extra words in a statement add meaning.

phrases.english: רב holds like רבי עקיבא,
who learns meaning from extra language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who treats extra words as adding meaning.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about selling a house with a pit and a cistern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its proof by quoting a משנה. Someone who sells a house does not sell the pit or cistern with it. According to רבי עקיבא, the seller must also buy a path to reach them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: [One who sells a house has not sold] the pit or the cistern, even if he wrote 'its depth and its height' in the sale document. And the seller must buy himself a path to reach them. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof for why רב's ruling follows רבי עקיבא. It starts by quoting the basic case and רבי עקיבא's ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit and a cistern are not part of the house, so they are not sold with it unless the sale names them. Even the phrase 'its depth and its height' does not include them. רבי עקיבא adds that the seller has no automatic right to walk across the buyer's land, so he must buy a path. This is only the background; the actual proof comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit dug in the ground to hold water.
A cistern, a built water tank.
Its depth and its height. Wording in a sale document that the sale goes down and up.
To buy himself a path, meaning the right to walk through the property.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: לֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת —
phrases.english: As we learned: [one who sells a house has sold] neither the pit nor the cistern —
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא בתרא 64a.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא.
phrases.english: even though he wrote to him 'its depth and its height.'
And he must buy himself a path,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller, who kept the pit and cistern.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim in Step 4 that רבי עקיבא holds extra words carry meaning.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי עקיבא gives meaning to extra, unneeded words, and that רב's ruling follows him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בבא בתרא 64a about selling a house without its pit and cistern.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees that 'except for these' gives the seller a path
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the seller never needs to buy a path. רבי עקיבא agrees with them when the seller said 'except for these.' Those words were not needed, so רבי עקיבא reads them as keeping a path too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He does not need to buy a path. And רבי עקיבא agrees that when the seller said to him 'except for these,' he does not need to buy a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. This is the line that actually proves רבי עקיבא gives meaning to extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pit and cistern were not sold anyway, so saying 'except for these' seems to add nothing. רבי עקיבא still treats those words as meaningful: they show that the seller kept the right to a path. This is the same idea as Step 3. There, saying 'and one day' as a separate addition created a second term of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי עקיבא here.
And he agrees. It shows a case where a תנא accepts the other side's ruling.
Except for these. The extra words the seller added about the pit and cistern.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא holds that words that were not needed still change the outcome. This is why רב rules that 'thirty days and one day' makes a person a נזיר twice. רב's ruling follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'except for these' is what keeps the pit and cistern for the seller. They were never part of the sale. That is exactly why the words count as extra, and why רבי עקיבא reads them as keeping a path.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line shows where רב's rule about 'thirty days and one day' comes from. Without רבי עקיבא's idea about extra words, 'and one day' would simply count as one longer term.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: He does not need to buy a path.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ
phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא agrees that when he said to him
'except for these,'
phrases.notes: 'These' means the pit and the cistern. They weren't being sold anyway, so these words were extra.

phrases.english: that he does not need to buy a path.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ חוּץ מֵאֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quoted in Step 5. Its concession clause is the proof point for Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא gives meaning to extra words, so רב's 'thirty days and one day' ruling follows his view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's agreement that the extra words 'except for these' give the seller a path without buying one.
